title: Koftos, Κοφτός, Grecia, tutorial di Juancarlos Battilani

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Juan Carlos Battilani teaches in an encouraging, structured manner, breaking down traditional Greek circle dances step-by-step with clear counting and verbal cues. He combines instructional explanations with full demonstrations to music, ensuring students understand both the footwork and the rhythm.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction of the teacher and the topic of Greek folk dance.
Introduction of the dance Koftos, explaining formation and general style.
Detailed breakdown of the 6-count sirtos steps to the right.
Explanation of the fourth sirtos ending with arms raised and a vocal cue.
Full practice of the dance steps to traditional music.

common_mistakes: Putting weight on the right foot too early on the fourth sirtos

steps_taught.name: Sirtos
steps_taught.description: Basic side step sequence moving to the right with arms in a closed circle.

what_works: Clear counting and repetition of steps
Demonstrating both slowly and to full music
what_hinders: Fixed overhead camera angle limits foot visibility

quotes.text: La danza che voglio presentarvi oggi si chiama Koftos.
Il modulo del sette ottavi è sempre slow, quick, quick, slow.
La teoria è tutta qui, andiamo a ballare Koftos.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher steps sideways demonstrating the first sirtos counting 1 to 6.
Teacher demonstrates raising arms and shouting Hey on the fourth count.
Teacher dances the full routine to music with consistent stepping.

extraction.distinctive_method: Combining verbal mnemonics of the rhythm (slow-quick-quick-slow) with direct numerical counts for each repetition.
